title: CRLR/183/2008 of SMT. TARANJEET KAUR and ANOTHER Vs STATE and ANOTHER

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.183 of 2008
Smt. Taranjeet Kaur and another ... Revisionists
vs.
State of Uttarakhand and another ... Respondents
Mr. B. S. Adhikari, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. P. S. Saun, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for respondent no.2.
Hon'ble U. C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
1. The revisionists, by means of present criminal revision,
seek to set-aside the impugned judgment and order dated
29.08.2008 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun in Criminal Case no.107 of 2006 titled as Smt.
Taranjeet Kaur & another vs. Amar Pal Singh under Section 125
Cr.P.C.. It is further prayed that respondent no.2 (Amar Pal
Singh/husband) may be directed to pay the maintenance
allowance to his wife (revisionist no.1) as well.
2. The revisionists filed an application under Section 125
Cr.P.C. against the respondent no.2 (Amar Pal Singh) for grant of
maintenance allowance. Respondent no.2 (husband of
revisionist no.1) filed written statement wherein he admitted his
marriage with revisionist no.1/Smt. Taranjeet Kaur. Oral and
documentary evidence was given by the parties. After
considering the evidence on record, the Principal Judge, Family
Court, Dehradun, vide order dated 29.08.2008, dismissed the
application of applicant no.1 (revisionist no.1 herein).
Respondent no.2 (husband) was, however, directed to pay a sum
of Rs.1500/- per month as maintenance allowance to his minor
son, i.e., applicant no.2 (revisionist no.2 herein).
3. Aggrieved against the same, present criminal revision was
moved by the revisionists.

-2-
4. Learned counsel for the revisionists assailed the findings of
the court below on the grounds, inter alia, that the court below
committed a mistake in holding that the allegations of dowry-demand against revisionist no.1's husband and his family
members were false, in as much as, a criminal case of harassment
in connection with demand of dowry is pending against the
husband (respondent no.2) and his parents in the court of
Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun. Learned counsel for the
revisionists further submitted that on an FIR lodged by the wife
(revisionist no.1), the matter was investigated and after
investigation of the case, a charge-sheet was submitted against
respondent no.2 (husband) and his family members under
Section 498-A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act. It
cannot, therefore, be said that the allegations of demand of
dowry were false. There is some sense in the contention of
learned counsel for the revisionists and it is, therefore, held that
the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun ought not to have
dismissed the application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. on this
ground.
5. But, there is also the other side of the coin. It has come on
evidence that the husband (respondent no.2 herein) is ready to
keep and maintain his wife (revisionist no.1), but the wife-revisionist is not willing to live with her husband, so long as his
parents and other family members live in the same house. Wife-revisionist no.1 said, in her cross examination that if her husband
lives separately from his parents and takes a rented house for her
and her child, then only she is willing to live with her husband.
Revisionist no.1 (wife) was also specific in saying that she is
unable to live with her husband, so long as he lives with his
parents and other family members in the joint family.
6. The wife (revisionist no.1) has further compounded the
problem for her by saying that she wants that her husband

-3-
(respondent no.2) should give the entire salary in her hands and
only then she will live with her husband.
7. Sub-section (4) to Section 125 Cr.P.C. provides as under:-
"125. Order for maintenance of wives, children and
parents. -
(4) No wife shall be entitled to receive an allowance for
the maintenance or the interim maintenance and
expenses of proceeding, as the case may be, from her
husband under this section if she is living in adultery, or
if, without any sufficient reason, she refuses to live with
her husband, or if they are living separately by mutual
consent."
8. Considering the facts of the case coupled with the
statement of wife (revisionist no.1), who says that she will live
with her husband only if a separate rented accommodation is
hired for her and her child, the parents and other family
members of her husband live separately and the husband should
give the entire salary in her hands, this Court is of the opinion
that the wife (revisionist no.1) wants to live with her husband-respondent no.2 only on her terms / dictates.
9. It appears that the revisionist-wife is living separately from
her husband without any sufficient reason, as was held by the
court below.
10. There is no illegality in the findings of learned court below
to this extent. No interference is called for in the impugned
judgment and order.
11. The Criminal Revision thus fails and is dismissed with the
observations as above.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.)
Dated 09th October, 2013 Rawat
